title: Sean McVay on defending against the Bills’ offense, decision-making, Week 5 injury report & more
headline: Aaron Donald is good to go and Colby Parkinson is cleared; Quentin Lake is questionable but trending up. A knee-surgery player will likely not have his IR clock started next week.
summary: McVay gave an injury update ahead of Monday's game against Buffalo. Aaron Donald was a DNP but is expected to play, with no game status assigned. Quentin Lake is the only player who will be listed as questionable, though McVay feels he is trending in the right direction. Colby Parkinson and another player referred to as 'Jalen' are cleared. McVay also discussed a player recovering from knee surgery, who is making good progress and is week-to-week. It is more likely than not that the team does not start that player's return clock next week, so he can fully recover. McVay distinguished return-to-play from return-to-performance, saying the player must hit benchmarks and football-related activities first. The lack of training camp practice was mainly due to knee irritation, which he expects to be resolved. On the Bills, McVay praised Josh Allen's growth in timing, rhythm, reading coverage and involving all eligible receivers, calling him a very special and difficult player to defend. He also discussed two-point conversion decisions, favoring getting the seven and keeping the game tied or with a chance to win, while stressing that analytics are one input among many and that game flow matters.
